name: esposter
description: A nice and casual place for posting random things.
author: Jimmy Chen

scripts.bench: vitest bench --run --project scripts && pnpm -r --if-present run bench
scripts.lint: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --disable-nested-config && virrun -- eslint . && virrun -- pnpm -r --parallel run lint
scripts.lint:fix: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --fix --disable-nested-config && virrun -- eslint --fix . && virrun -- pnpm -r --parallel run lint:fix
scripts.lint:fix:packages: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --fix --disable-nested-config packages && virrun -- pnpm -r --filter "./packages/*" --parallel run lint:fix
scripts.lint:packages: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --disable-nested-config packages && virrun -- pnpm -r --filter "./packages/*" --parallel run lint
scripts.release: pnpm format:check && pnpm build:packages && pnpm lint:packages && pnpm typecheck:packages && pnpm test:packages && lerna publish --yes
scripts.typecheck: virrun -- tsc && virrun -- pnpm -r --parallel run typecheck

scriptsComments.build: A deviation taken on purpose: the bare name means the whole workspace in a pnpm, turbo or nx repo alike, and here it means the web app plus the libraries it imports, because Railway runs `pnpm build` as its default build command. That makes this name a deploy entrypoint rather than a developer convenience, and widening it would have every deploy build two bundles it never ships. Two selectors, both derived rather than named. `--filter "@esposter/web^..."` is everything the app imports, in topological order, so nothing here knows which libraries exist. `--filter "{.}^..."` is what the root itself depends on, which is where the toolchain is declared — `virrun` above all, whose committed `bin/cli.js` imports a `dist` only its own build writes. The app does not import it, so the first selector cannot reach it, and a deploy that builds from source rather than from CI's `package-builds` artifact then dies inside `build:web` on `Cannot find module '.../packages/virrun/dist/cli.js'`. That is the whole reason for the second selector: here the toolchain is a build input, not a dependency. `^...` rather than the `{.}...` that `setup-packages` installs, because this one is a `run` — matching the root would have `build` recurse into itself. The two halves stay separate commands because only the second one belongs in the sandbox — a library's output is platform-neutral and read from host disk, so `virrun` would charge it the mirror tax for an isolation nothing wants, while the app build is the one that needs the Linux-generated `.nuxt` (see the virrun adoption page). `build:packages` is a third set: every library rather than the ones this app imports, which is what CI caches and hands to the checks, and the coverage shards build the two apps whose bundles the suite asserts against. @TODO: restore `pnpm build:docs` to the chain when a bridge build grows the AST navigation API. TypeDoc exits 6 against the `typescript-native-bridge` alias, and `build` is what deploy runs, so the deploy would fail on documentation alone. `build:docs` stays as the probe. See the `build-docs` job in .github/workflows/CI.yaml.
